rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.1-2.2, a two-year (2019-2020) field experiment at the Shuguang Experimental Station in the Hetao Irrigation District with five mulching x irrigation treatments in a randomized block design, reporting own measurements of soil/canopy humidity, temperature, photosynthesis, yield and economics.
rows.notes: The study does report that plastic film mulching reduced diurnal soil temperature amplitude (Fig. 5; FT, FB, DT 1.1, 0.8, 1.3 C lower than FN in 2019) and raised canopy air relative humidity (Fig. 2; mulched treatments 4-6% higher than DN), but the irrigation method was border irrigation (Section 2.2: 'The irrigation method was border irrigation', 500 mm full vs 300 mm deficit applied in four applications). No drip irrigation was tested, so the result is about transparent/black film mulch under border irrigation, not drip irrigation under plastic mulch (DIPM) as the passage claims. Technology mismatch; Q2 answered no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a primary field experiment on plastic film mulch with full vs deficit border irrigation for spring maize; it contains no drip irrigation treatment.
